newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli army officer punished for Rabin letters.
newsitem.headline: Israeli army officer punished for Rabin letters.

text.p: An Israeli military court has reduced an officer in rank for threatening letters he sent to Yitzhak Rabin before the prime minister was assassinated, Israel's Itim news agency said on Wednesday.

Israel Channel One Television said Areyeh Bar-Yosef, a religious Jew who appeared on its Friday news programme and welcomed Rabin's murder was indicted in a Jerusalem court on Wednesday on charges of sedition and supporting a terrorist organisation after comments he made on the programme.
The reports came as concern increased in Israel a year after Rabin's assassination that Jewish militants may strike again over a government's plan to hand land to Palestinians.

Itim said a military court in Haifa in northern Israel ordered Major Daniel Bevis, 37, be reduced in rank to lieutenant. It rejected the prosecution's call Bevis be made a private and sentenced to a jail term.
A week ago, the court had convicted Bevis on three counts of unbecoming conduct. The charges arose in part from letters Bevis sent to Rabin in January 1994, Itim said.
"You are a rag, you socialise with evildoers for whom Jewish blood is like water. You will pay for this," Itim quoted one of the letters as saying.

Itim said those under Bevis's command also quoted him saying: "Rabin conspired with the wanted man Arafat to drink our blood" and "Rabin is a murderer, Rabin is a traitor, this government has to be brought down at any price."

Rabin's government signed interim peace deals with Yasser Arafat's Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) that provided Palestinian self-rule in parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip, areas Israel occupied in the 1967 Middle East war.
Bevis was also quoted as praising settler Baruch Goldstein who massacred 29 Palestinians in the West Bank town of Hebron in February 1994. Survivors beat Goldstein to death.
A right-wing religious Jew gunned down Rabin on November 4, 1995, in Tel Aviv. Assassin Yigal Amir said he shot Rabin to prevent him handing land to the Palestinians.
Israel's previous government agreed in a deal with the PLO a year ago to withdraw from six West Bank towns and partly from Hebron, the only one of the seven with Jews living inside it.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who opposes trading occupied land for peace, won a general election last May. But he has said he would honour deals, such as the one on Hebron, signed by the previous government. Militants describe the deal as betrayal.
